issue.title: gateway/antigravity: a reply restarted inside one Code Assist SSE stream reaches the agent spliced (gemini-4-argon, since 2026-10-21)
issue.body:
## Summary

Since 2026-10-21T22:21Z, some `gemini-4-argon` replies served through the Antigravity provider (Code Assist upstream) reach the agent as **one** chat completion whose text is two to four differently worded partial answers glued end to end. magpie's own ledger shows one try and one upstream request for every such reply, so the restarts happen **inside one upstream SSE response**; the Code Assist decoder passes each generation's text parts through as deltas and only reads `responseId` on the first chunk, so nothing tells the client that the reply started over.

Observed on 0.1.1267. In 0.1.1293 (`b641868`) `internal/gateway/codeassist.go` is byte-identical and `continuation.go` differs only in usage accounting, so the behaviour should be the same.

## Setup

- macOS arm64, magpie 0.1.1267 (desktop app), Antigravity provider with one Google AI Ultra account
- model `antigravity/gemini-4-argon`, `reasoning_effort: high`
- client: Pi 1.3.0 (`openai-completions`, `stream: true`) on `/v1/chat/completions`, i.e. `/v1/chat/completions → /v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`
- 11 cases from 4 agents between 2026-10-21T22:36Z and 2026-10-22T07:45Z; prompts from 10k to 636k tokens (mostly cached), so it is not tied to context length

## Symptom (shortest case)

One completion, 224 characters, `finish_reason: stop`, 42.7 s, 111 output tokens. Byte offsets of the four segments:

```
@0    在（provider: `kota-local`，model: `magpie/antigr
@46   在！本金刚当前 provider 为 `kota-local`，模型为 `magpie/antigravity/
@102  在（provider：`kota-local`，模型：`magpie/antigravity/gemini
@155  在（provider: `kota-local`，model: `magpie/antigravity/gemini-4-argon`）。
```

Each segment is a fresh generation of the same answer, cut at a different point; only the last one is complete. The larger cases are 5k–19k characters with 2–4 segments. In two of them every segment begins with `Thinking Process:` written as plain text (those rows count 0 reasoning tokens, i.e. the upstream returned no `thought` parts at all for that reply).

## Why it is one upstream response

For the case above, `usage.jsonl` has one row: `in 2049, out 111, ms 42663, ttft_ms 16654, first_text_ms 16654, flow_ms 23816, status 200`, and the matching `routing/<date>.jsonl` record has `tries: 1` with `net.asks: 1`. `nettrace.go` counts every `GetConn` of the try, including a request asked again in place (TryNet: "Asks counts them all, the last one too"), and the try's context is the one `streamTranslated` → `forwardTranslated` use, so any re-ask by the continuation, the empty-reply or the loop path would show `asks ≥ 2`. All nine visibly spliced replies have `tries 1 / asks 1`, and the client saw one HTTP response with one `chatcmpl-…` id.

So the generations were restarted upstream within the single SSE stream, and magpie forwarded each one's text.

## Fingerprint in the ledger

- `in` (promptTokenCount − cachedContentTokenCount) is **exactly 2049** on every such row: the restarted generation hits the implicit cache of the prompt that was just sent. `out` is the sum over all segments (111 tokens for the 224-character example above), and `flow_ms/out` is 18–326 ms/token against ≤ 15 ms/token for normal replies of the same model.
- 15 antigravity rows carry this fingerprint, all `gemini-4-argon`, all between 2026-10-21T22:21Z and 2026-10-22T07:44Z; 0 of the 770 antigravity rows of the 12 days before. Nine of the 15 are visibly spliced; the rest are tool-call-only replies where it cannot be seen in the text. In that window roughly a third to a half of the model's text replies were affected.

## Code reading (`b641868`, same lines in `a15e576`)

- `continuation.go:205` `prefillHow` returns `""` for Code Assist, so `continuation.possible()` is false and a cut stream ends with `errEndedShort` (`:561`, `:649`). That path works as intended — one unrelated reply in the same window ended with `Antigravity: the reply ended before it was complete` and was **not** spliced.
- The empty-reply re-ask and the loop re-ask only fire before anything was said; `holdWriter.mayAskAgain` requires that nothing reached the agent; `textCallSee` only holds text from a `<tool_call>` / DSML mark. None of them applies once text has been sent.
- `codeassist.go:838` `decode` → `:877` iterates candidates and parts → `:910` `d.text()` emits `KText` at once. `:875` reads `ResponseID` only on the first chunk (`geminiChunk` carries it, `:1199`). A later chunk with a different `responseId`, a `usageMetadata.candidatesTokenCount` lower than the one before, or parts arriving after a `finishReason` are not noticed.

## Suggested handling

In `codeAssistDecoder.decode`, remember the first chunk's `responseId` (and the last `candidatesTokenCount`); when a later chunk shows a different `responseId`, a lower count, or content after the stop, treat the reply as restarted:

- if nothing has been said yet, drop what came and go on, as the empty-reply path does;
- otherwise stop reading and end the reply with an error in the client's protocol, as `errEndedShort` does, so the agent asks again instead of showing two answers glued together. A wording agents classify as retryable would let them recover on their own (Pi retries on `service unavailable` / `overloaded` / 5xx, not on "ended before it was complete").

Marking such rows in `usage.jsonl` would also help users find affected turns.

I could not get the raw upstream bodies for these calls (Recent calls had rotated by the time I looked). If it helps I can capture one from the next occurrence, and I am happy to test a build.

comments.body:
Two corrections and a few more data points, from a colleague who went through the client session files independently:

- In the JSON above, the 5,835-character case with an empty `segment_starts_by_repeated_opening` restarts at offset **3013**, not 2946 as I wrote; the 5,220-character case has **four** segments (1140 / 2369 / 3724), the later two reworded so the repeated-opening heuristic missed them.
- Two fingerprint rows (`in == 2049`) are not visibly spliced but fit the same picture: one reply with 11.5k characters of reasoning and a text of a single newline after 9.6 minutes, and one coherent 1,643-character reply that took 175 s for 1,069 output tokens (about 164 ms/token), i.e. pauses between restarts without a visible seam.
- After the last hit at 2026-10-22T07:44Z, the next 58 `gemini-4-argon` replies through this gateway (up to 08:27Z, five of them with text) show neither the fingerprint nor a splice, so the upstream behaviour looks intermittent rather than permanent.
- The `Thinking Process:` text mentioned above turned out to be the model imitating an earlier such reply inside one long session (17 of 18 replies in that session, 0 of 41 in other sessions); unrelated to this issue.

Confirmed in the decoder, as you put it: `codeAssistDecoder` read `responseId` only on the first chunk and then passed every generation's text parts through as deltas of the same answer, so a restart inside one SSE response could only arrive spliced.

Fixed on [fix/3248-codeassist-restart](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3248-codeassist-restart) (`db55f831`, one commit on `01468003`). The decoder now remembers the generation it is reading - its `responseId`, the highest `candidatesTokenCount` it reached, whether a `finishReason` has ended it, and whether anything of it was already emitted - and treats a chunk as a new generation when the `responseId` changed, the token count went back, or content arrives after the `finishReason`:

- if the aborted generation had already reached the client, the reply is ended there with a `503` whose text says Antigravity restarted mid-answer and the request should be asked again; the rest of the stream is dropped. Splicing two answers into one was the alternative, and that is what #2243 was refused for: the protocol has no way to say "a second answer starts here", so a client would keep the abandoned prefix.
- if nothing of it had been emitted, the abandoned prefix is discarded and the generation that restarted is read as the answer - the same choice the empty-reply path already makes.

RED -> GREEN, re-run independently here:
- clean base + only the new test file: `TestCodeAssistRestartIsNotSpliced` fails on all three shapes with both generations' text, e.g. `one answer has both generations' text: "Provider is Provider is kota-local, and the model is argon."`
- at the head: the same test passes (new `responseId`, token count gone back, content after `finishReason`), including the case where nothing had reached the client yet.
- full `go test ./internal/gateway` passes except `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, which is red on the clean base too; `go vet` and `go build` for linux, windows and `-tags nogui` pass; `gofmt -l` is empty.

Limits: the chunk shapes are reconstructed from your ledger, not a captured upstream body (you did not have one either), and no real `gemini-4-argon` call was made. Whether a given client automatically retries after an in-stream 503 was not measured - the change only guarantees such a reply can no longer look like one coherent answer. If you would rather keep the last complete generation and end `finish_reason: stop` on it, that is a one-line difference in the same place, but it would silently drop the prefix the agent already saw, so the error was chosen.

- The `Thinking Process:` text mentioned above turned out to be the model imitating an earlier such reply inside one long session (17 of 18 replies in that session, 0 of 41 in other sessions); unrelated to this issue.

Confirmed in the decoder, as you put it: `codeAssistDecoder` read `responseId` only on the first chunk and then passed every generation's text parts through as deltas of the same answer, so a restart inside one SSE response could only arrive spliced.

Fixed on [fix/3248-codeassist-restart](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3248-codeassist-restart) (`db55f831`, one commit on `01468003`). The decoder now remembers the generation it is reading - its `responseId`, the highest `candidatesTokenCount` it reached, whether a `finishReason` has ended it, and whether anything of it was already emitted - and treats a chunk as a new generation when the `responseId` changed, the token count went back, or content arrives after the `finishReason`:

- if the aborted generation had already reached the client, the reply is ended there with a `503` whose text says Antigravity restarted mid-answer and the request should be asked again; the rest of the stream is dropped. Splicing two answers into one was the alternative, and that is what #2243 was refused for: the protocol has no way to say "a second answer starts here", so a client would keep the abandoned prefix.
- if nothing of it had been emitted, the abandoned prefix is discarded and the generation that restarted is read as the answer - the same choice the empty-reply path already makes.

RED -> GREEN, re-run independently here:
- clean base + only the new test file: `TestCodeAssistRestartIsNotSpliced` fails on all three shapes with both generations' text, e.g. `one answer has both generations' text: "Provider is Provider is kota-local, and the model is argon."`
- at the head: the same test passes (new `responseId`, token count gone back, content after `finishReason`), including the case where nothing had reached the client yet.
- full `go test ./internal/gateway` passes except `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`, which is red on the clean base too; `go vet` and `go build` for linux, windows and `-tags nogui` pass; `gofmt -l` is empty.

Limits: the chunk shapes are reconstructed from your ledger, not a captured upstream body (you did not have one either), and no real `gemini-4-argon` call was made. Whether a given client automatically retries after an in-stream 503 was not measured - the change only guarantees such a reply can no longer look like one coherent answer. If you would rather keep the last complete generation and end `finish_reason: stop` on it, that is a one-line difference in the same place, but it would silently drop the prefix the agent already saw, so the error was chosen.

issue.title: Antigravity / Gemini 4 Argon：工具调用被上游写进正文，长会话反复出现重复答案（双侧 SSE 对照）

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 现象

Windows 上使用 Magpie `v0.1.2729`，通过 Anthropic 兼容的 `/v1/messages` 调用 `antigravity/gemini-4-argon-high`。在一段长会话里，用户会看到一份工具参数 JSON，随后又看到一遍正式答案。客户端收到的是普通正文，工具列表为空。这个问题会影响展示，也会把工具调用样式的文字留给后续轮次。

## 同一笔请求的双侧 SSE 对照

用该版本源码的隔离诊断构建，在 Code Assist 响应进入 Magpie 解码器前复制响应体，同时在客户端记录 Magpie 发出的 SSE。确认只有一笔客户端 POST、一次成功的上游生成请求和一个 Google response ID。上游读到 EOF，下游收到 `message_stop`。以下是事件结构和计数，未附用户输入、回复正文或原始请求。

| | Google Code Assist → Magpie | Magpie → Anthropic 协议客户端 |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP / 完成原因 | 200，`STOP` | 200，`end_turn` |
| SSE 事件 | 119 个 | 123 个 |
| 可见内容 | 119 个 `parts[].text`（含末尾空片段），0 个 `functionCall`，0 个带 `thought: true` 的文本片段 | 1 个 `text` 块，118 个 `text_delta`，0 个 `tool_use` |
| 工具名、参数 JSON 已经位于正文 | 第 46–47 个事件 | 第 48–49 个事件 |
| 文本形式的“执行完毕”标记和重复答案 | 第 81–82 个事件起 | 第 83–84 个事件起 |

按事件顺序拼接双方的可见文本，共 5,458 个字符。保留空格、换行和 Unicode 原样，两端 UTF-8 字节完全相同，SHA-256 也相同。正文参数 JSON 中的 `result` 在后面的答案中再次完整出现（忽略标点和空白）。因此，这次复现中，伪工具调用文本已经由 Google 返回，Magpie 的响应转换保留了原文。

## 触发条件和对照

- 用原长会话在故障提问处重放，排除了那一轮的异常答案及之后的消息。此前已有助手回复包含相同样式的伪工具记录。原历史请求没有逐字节留存；重放恢复了 26 个工具定义，历史路由摘要折算为 54 个。
- 简短上下文下，同一路由曾返回正常的 `tool_use` 和 `input_json_delta`。所以只发一句短提示，未必能复现。
- 在一次额外的隔离对照里，只清理历史助手消息中 39 条能核对为“伪完成工具包装＋重复答案”的记录，保留正式答案、用户消息、真实工具调用和结果。同账号、同模型、同问题再次返回正常正文，没有伪工具调用。这是一次对照，尚不能据此确定触发条件或发生率。

## 建议的处理方式

1. **先加诊断。** Antigravity 路由收到纯文本、其中出现完整伪调用包装时，可记录命中的类型及计数，方便和真正的 `functionCall` 区分；诊断本身无需记录正文。
2. **优先在下一轮整理发往上游的助手历史。** 仅当历史助手消息没有真实工具调用、完成工具的参数 JSON 能按已知 schema 解析、文本中有明确的包装结束边界，并且后续独立答案和 `result` 高度一致时，才考虑在该路由的请求副本中只保留最终答案。保留用户输入、结构化工具调用及工具结果；仅凭工具名或 JSON 片段不应触发清理。
3. **如要保护当前轮的流式显示，可做成可选策略。** 已发给客户端的增量无法撤回；若选择暂存疑似包装，应有缓冲上限，证据不足时原样放行。不要把正文中模仿出来的调用提升为可执行工具，尤其是有副作用的工具。
4. **回归测试可使用合成 SSE。** 用无关占位文字构造“可见文本中的伪完成调用＋重复答案”，让工具名、JSON 和结束边界分别跨 chunk；再测正常 `functionCall`、普通代码块中的调用示例、参数和最终答案不同这三类反例。这样无需真实会话也能验证保护逻辑。

相关但表现有差异：#636 涉及文本形式调用与工具块缺失；#3248 涉及同一流中多段答案拼接。此处同时核对了 Google 和 Magpie 两侧的事件类型及可见文本。
